newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen weaker at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen weaker at open.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Monday after a strong day on Friday, and traders said the market would likely be on hold ahead of Tuesday's release of U.S. and Canadian consumer price data.

"I think we'll have a bit of downer at the opening, although it's hard to tell. Europe is very much weaker, the U.S. dollar is weaker, but it looks like U.S. stocks are slightly higher along with the bonds, so it's mixed signals," one trader said.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index rose 35 points on Friday to reach its 18th record close of the year.
The trader said Friday's triple-witching -- when options, futures, and options on futures all expire -- will add volatility to North American markets this week.
"This week is triple witch, which will do a pretty good job on any real market trend, just the expiry will give us volatility that we don't normally have," he said.
He said investors would keep their eyes on tomorrow's Consumer Price Index data due out on both sides of the border as an indication of when the U.S. Federal Reserve might hike interest rates.
Interest-sensitive stocks rallied last week after softer-than-expected U.S. producer price index and retail sales data likely ruled out a rate increase at the Fed's next meeting on July 1-2.
* Bombardier Corp is expected to announce this week a US$1.2 billion order from AMR Corp for 67 of its 50-seat regional jets.
